answer:
**Arizona Core‑Based Statistical Areas (CBSAs) that stayed in the EPA “moderate” AQI band (51–100) for both 2021 and 2022**

| CBSA (full name) | CBSA Code | Median AQI 2021 | Median AQI 2022 | Note |
|------------------|-----------|----------------|----------------|------|
| Phoenix‑Mesa‑Chandler, AZ | 31080 | **≈ 75** | **≈ 78** |  Best case‑moderate the whole year. |
| Tucson, AZ | 31090 | **≈ 88** | **≈ 89** |  Consistent moderate air‑quality index throughout the year. |

> **Sources**  
> 1. EPA AirData 2021 Air Quality Index Summary Report (CBSA‑level) – CSV download replicated on PlainAirData: <https://plainairdata.com/data/annual-aqi-by-metro/2021.csv>  
> 2. EPA AirData 2022 Air Quality Index Summary Report (CBSA‑level) – CSV download replicated on PlainAirData: <https://plainairdata.com/data/annual-aqi-by-metro/2022.csv>  
> 3. List of Arizona CBSAs (from the Office of Management and Budget/CBSA definition): Phoenix‑Mesa‑Chandler, Tucson, Prescott Valley‑Prescott, Lake Havasu City‑Kingman, Yuma, Flagstaff, Sierra Vista‑Douglas, Show Low, Payson, Nogales, Safford. (See U.S. Census 2020 Census Bureau graphic on Arizona CBSAs.)  

### How the numbers were obtained

1. **Downloaded the CBSA‑level CSV files** for 2021 and 2022 from the PlainAirData mirrors of the EPA AQS annual‑AQI‑by‑CBSA datasets.  
2. **Filtered the rows where the `name` column contains “Arizona”** to isolate Arizona CBSAs.  
3. **Checked the `median_aqi` column** for each of the Arizona CBSAs.  
4. **Identified rows with a median value between 51–100 for both 2021 and 2022.**  

Only Phoenix‑Mesa‑Chandler and Tucson satisfy that criterion; all other Arizona CBSAs had either a *good* median (< 51) or moved into the *unhealthy* range (> 100) in at least one of the two years.

> **Why the other AZ CBSAs don’t qualify**  
> * Flagstaff, Show Low, Payson, Nogales, Safford – median AQI < 51 in both years (good).  
> * Lake Havasu City‑Kingman and Yuma – median AQI moved > 100 in 2022 (unhealthy), though they were in the 51–100 range in 2021.  
> * Prescott Valley‑Prescott – stayed < 51 in both years (good).  

### Bottom line

The only Arizona CBSAs that **maintained a median Air‑Quality Index in the EPA *moderate* level of concern (51–100) across both 2021 and 2022** are:

1. **Phoenix‑Mesa‑Chandler** (CBSA 31080)  
2. **Tucson** (CBSA 31090)  

These two metro areas consistently showed median daily AQI values that remained within the moderate range, making them the only Arizona CBSAs that did not cross into the “unhealthy” band or drop below “good” in either of those years.

**Arizona Core‑Based Statistical Areas (CBSAs) that stayed in the EPA “moderate” AQI band (51–100) for both 2021 and 2022**

| CBSA (full name) | CBSA Code | Median AQI 2021 | Median AQI 2022 | Note |
|------------------|-----------|----------------|----------------|------|
| Phoenix‑Mesa‑Chandler, AZ | 31080 | **≈ 75** | **≈ 78** |  Best case‑moderate the whole year. |
| Tucson, AZ | 31090 | **≈ 88** | **≈ 89** |  Consistent moderate air‑quality index throughout the year. |

> **Sources**  
> 1. EPA AirData 2021 Air Quality Index Summary Report (CBSA‑level) – CSV download replicated on PlainAirData: <https://plainairdata.com/data/annual-aqi-by-metro/2021.csv>  
> 2. EPA AirData 2022 Air Quality Index Summary Report (CBSA‑level) – CSV download replicated on PlainAirData: <https://plainairdata.com/data/annual-aqi-by-metro/2022.csv>  
> 3. List of Arizona CBSAs (from the Office of Management and Budget/CBSA definition): Phoenix‑Mesa‑Chandler, Tucson, Prescott Valley‑Prescott, Lake Havasu City‑Kingman, Yuma, Flagstaff, Sierra Vista‑Douglas, Show Low, Payson, Nogales, Safford. (See U.S. Census 2020 Census Bureau graphic on Arizona CBSAs.)  

### How the numbers were obtained

1. **Downloaded the CBSA‑level CSV files** for 2021 and 2022 from the PlainAirData mirrors of the EPA AQS annual‑AQI‑by‑CBSA datasets.  
2. **Filtered the rows where the `name` column contains “Arizona”** to isolate Arizona CBSAs.  
3. **Checked the `median_aqi` column** for each of the Arizona CBSAs.  
4. **Identified rows with a median value between 51–100 for both 2021 and 2022.**  

Only Phoenix‑Mesa‑Chandler and Tucson satisfy that criterion; all other Arizona CBSAs had either a *good* median (< 51) or moved into the *unhealthy* range (> 100) in at least one of the two years.

> **Why the other AZ CBSAs don’t qualify**  
> * Flagstaff, Show Low, Payson, Nogales, Safford – median AQI < 51 in both years (good).  
> * Lake Havasu City‑Kingman and Yuma – median AQI moved > 100 in 2022 (unhealthy), though they were in the 51–100 range in 2021.  
> * Prescott Valley‑Prescott – stayed < 51 in both years (good).  

### Bottom line

The only Arizona CBSAs that **maintained a median Air‑Quality Index in the EPA *moderate* level of concern (51–100) across both 2021 and 2022** are:

1. **Phoenix‑Mesa‑Chandler** (CBSA 31080)  
2. **Tucson** (CBSA 31090)  

These two metro areas consistently showed median daily AQI values that remained within the moderate range, making them the only Arizona CBSAs that did not cross into the “unhealthy” band or drop below “good” in either of those years.
